Bikash Paul, Advocate—For the Petitioners. 
Bivuti Tarofder, Advocate—For the Respondent No. 2.
parties:
Suruj Molla (Md) and another ---- Petitioners
VS
Artha Rin Adalat and others ----- Respondents
full_judgment:
Md Mozibur Rahman Miah, J: At the instance of the judgment debtors in Artha Execution Case No. 23 of 2018 and that of the defendants in Artha Rin Suit No. 7 of 2014, this Rule Nisi was issued in the following terms: 

 "Let a Rule Nisi be issued calling upon the respondents to show cause as to why the order dated 18-11-2020 passed by the respondent No. 1 in Miscellaneous Case No. 4 of 2020, arising out of Artha Rin Suit No. 7 of 2014 recalling the order dated 16-9-2020 passed in Miscellaneous Case No. 4 of 2020 shall not be declared to have been passed without lawful authority and is of no legal effect and /or pass such other or further order or orders passed as to this Court may seem fit and proper." 

 2. At the time of issuance of the Rule, this court also stayed the operation of the impugned order dated 18-11-2020 passed by the respondent No. 1 in Miscellaneous Case No. 4 of 2020 for a period of 6(six) months. However, on the date of issuance of the Rule, this court also fixed the matter for passing further order fixing it on 12-12-2021. Record shows that, no further extension was taken of the operation of the impugned order. 

 The present respondent No.2 as plaintiff originally filed a suit being Artha Rin Suit No. 7 of 2014 against the present petitioners impleading them as defendants in the said suit claiming an amount of Taka 6,67,011 as of outstanding dues. As the defendants did not appear the suit was ultimately decreed ex-parte on 26-8-2014 (decreed drawn up on 31-8-2014). Since the defendants did not repay the decretal dues, the present respondent No. 2 then filed an Execution Case being Artha Execution Case No. 33 of 2014 which was subsequently renumbered as Artha Execution Case No. 23 of 2018. Near about 6 years of decreeing the suit, the present petitioners on 16-9-2020 filed an application under section 19(1)(2)(3) and (4) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 (precisely "the Ain") for setting aside the ex-parte decree claiming that, they came to learn about the said decree on 15-9-2020 and on the following day they filed the application which gave rise to Miscellaneous Case No. 4 of 2020. On the very date of filing the said Miscellaneous case, the learned judge, respondent No. 1 allowed the same (dated 16-9-2020). After that, the present respondent No. 2 on 29-10-2020 filed an application for setting aside the said restoration order for ends of justice. Against that very application for setting aside the restoration order, the present petitioners on 4-11-2020 also filed written objection. The learned judge however vide impugned order dated 18-11-2020 allowed the application of the bank and thus set aside the restoration order passed by him on 16-9-2020. 

 5. Mr Bikash Paul, the learned counsel appearing for the petitioners upon taking us to the writ petition and all the annexure so appended therewith at the very outset submits that, since under the provision of section 19(2) of the Ain the petitioners filed the application by depositing 10% of the decretal amount through pay order so the court has nothing to do but to restore the suit and in the instant case, the learned judge vide order dated 16-9-2020 rightly restored the suit to its original filed and number by setting aside the ex-parte judgment and decree passed on 31-8-2014. 

 6. The learned counsel next contends that, since under the provision of section 41 of the Ain any order passed by the Artha Rin Adalat can only be challenged through preferring appeal and in case of preferring appeal, the bank is not required to deposit any amount, so without exhausting that alternative and efficacious remedy it field the application for setting aside the restoration order in the pretext of ends of justice which cannot be sustained in law. 

 9. The learned counsel next contends that, in the meantime the petitioners have repaid 50% of the claim amount to the respondent No. 2 yet the respondent No. 2 kept on proceeding with the execution case for realizing the decretal dues which is totally illegal illogical and cannot be sustained. With such submission the learned counsel finally prays for making the Rule absolute. 

 10. On the flipside, Mr Bivuti Tarofder, the learned counsel appearing for the respondent No. 2 by filing an affidavit-in-opposition very candidly opposes the submission so placed by the learned counsel for the petitioners and contends that, since the petitioners entered appearance upon receiving summons and took adjournment for filing written statement so there has been no occasion to claim that they came to learn about the ex-parte decree through information slip which is barefaced untrue and adopted for delay the disposal of the execution case. The learned counsel by annexing entire order sheets of Artha Rin Suit No.7 of 2014 draws our attention to order nos. 5 and 6 dated 4-6-2014 and 1-7-2014 respectively further submits that, from those two orders it is crystal clear that, having every knowledge about the proceedings of the suit, they have cooked up a story in their application filed under section 19 of the Ain for setting aside the ex-parte decree and therefore the learned judge has rightly exercised his inherent jurisdiction under section 57 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain and set aside the restoration order he passed earlier on 16-9-2020. 

 11. The learned counsel also contends that, since the petitioners claimed that they came to learn about the said ex-parte decree through filing a "mention slip" so heavy burden lies upon them to prove the date of knowledge by adducing and producing evidence but it has not been done still the learned judge on the following date of filing the miscellaneous case set aside the ex-parte decree on 16-9-2020 which was ex-facie illegal. 

 15. We have considered the submission so placed by the learned counsel for the petitioners and that of the respondent No. 2. Only point-in-issue revolves around to dispose of the instant Rule is, whether the provision of section 57 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain will be applicable in setting aside restoration order passed by the respondent No. 1 and whether against the order of setting aside the ex-parte decree, the respondent No. 2 ought to have preferred an appeal under section 41 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain. To address those two vital issues, we at the first place feel it expedient to see the application filed for restoration which has been annexed as Annexure-'F' to the writ petition. On going through paragraph No. 4 as well as paragraph No. 8 thereof, we find that, it has been alleged therein that, no notice or summons has ever been served upon the petitioners and they just came to learn about the ex-parte decree by filing information slip on 15-9-2020 and on the following day i.e, on 16-9-2020 they filed the Miscellaneous case. In that aspect we feel to examine the order sheets of Artha Rin Suit No. 7 of 2014 which has been annexed by the present respondent No. 2 as of Annexure-'2' to its -affidavit-in-opposition. On going through the orders being orders dated 4-6-2014 and 1-7-2014 we find that, the summons had duly been served upon the petitioners and the petitioners entered their appearance by filing a new power. The petitioners can not claim that they were not aware about the said orders passed by the Artha Rin Adalat because when they filed the Miscellaneous case under section 19 of the Ain they got the opportunity to go through the order sheets. Had it been so, then the alleged assertion so made out in the application for setting aside the ex-parte decree is proved to be totally untrue and on that score we genuinely assume that, fraud has been practiced upon the court for getting the ex-parte order set aside. Moreover, on the date of filing the Miscellaneous case the learned judge did not feel it bothered to issue summons or notice upon the respondent bank enabling it to appear and contest the case rather on the very date of filing the Miscellaneous case it was allowed which sounds totally unusual. 

 16. We have also very meticulously gone through the decision so have been reported in 66 DLR 1 and in paragraph No. 13 thereof, it has clearly been spelt out that, in case of basing on date of knowledge while filing Miscellaneous case, the defendant petitioner must adduce and produce witness to prove the date of knowledge. But in the instant case it has not been done and the learned judge restored the suit in its original file and number even without bothering to inform the respondent No. 2 bank. In such a circumstances, it can easily construe that, the petitioners have misguided the learned judge of the Artha Rin Adalat in obtaining the order setting aside the ex-parte decree. In such a situation it is our considered view that, the provision of section 57 of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain will come into play and the respondent No. 1 has perfectly exercised his inherent jurisdiction in setting aside the restoration order of the suit apparently fraud has been practiced in obtaining the order. Now let us address the point in regard to preferring appeal claimed to be filed by the respondent No. 2 against the order setting aside the restoration order but we don't find any iota of substance in the said submission so placed by the learned counsel for the petitioners. Because, that very provision for preferring appeal under section 41 of the Ain is only applicable if it is against any judgment and decree passed by the Artha Rin Adalat not against any interim order. And for that obvious reason, the provision of section 44(2) has been incorporated in the Artha Rin Ain which runs as follows: 

 20. The learned judge respondent No. 1 is hereby directed to proceed with the Execution Case No. 23 of 2018 and dispose of the same as expeditiously as possible preferably within 2(two) months from the date of receipt of the copy of this order.
